meta.name: LevelBridge starter data
meta.subject: Science (Class 1-10 continuous ladder)
meta.note: Starter content written with AI help. A teacher must review it against the school's own textbook before classroom use.

levels.name: Living and non-living, body parts

teacherActivity.title: Nature walk and senses check
steps: Take students into the schoolyard to observe living plants/insects and non-living stones/benches.
Categorize items into two columns on a slate: 'Needs food & grows' vs 'Does not grow'.
Point to eyes, ears, nose, tongue, skin to review the five sense organs.

levels.selfPractice: Draw two living things and two non-living things in drawing notebook.

levels.name: Animals, habitats, food, water, air

teacherActivity.title: Animal home and diet sorting
steps: Sort animal picture cards into habitats: Land, Water, Sky/Trees.
Sort cards by diet: Plant-eaters (herbivores) vs Flesh-eaters (carnivores).
Demonstrate that air is all around by trapping it in an inflated balloon.

levels.selfPractice: Match animals to their homes (e.g. bird -> nest, dog -> kennel, fish -> pond).

levels.name: Plant parts, food groups, soil, light

teacherActivity.title: Uprooted weed inspection and plate balancing
steps: Examine a real potted plant: identify taproot, fibrous roots, stem, leaves, and flower buds.
Sort meal items (rice, dal, spinach, milk) into energy-giving, body-building, and protective food groups.
Show how light travels in a straight line using cardboard holes and a flashlight.

levels.selfPractice: Label parts of a plant diagram (Root, Stem, Leaf, Flower) on a worksheet.

levels.name: Body systems intro, adaptation, states of matter

teacherActivity.title: Three states with ice and water
steps: Show ice cube melting into liquid water, and boil a drop to show water vapor (solid, liquid, gas).
Discuss animal adaptations: why camels have broad padded feet and polar bears have blubber.
Trace breathing cycle: nose -> windpipe -> lungs expanding.

levels.selfPractice: Classify listed materials (wood, oil, steam, pebble, juice) into Solid, Liquid, or Gas.

levels.name: Digestion, materials, simple machines

teacherActivity.title: Ruler lever and digestive pathway
steps: Use a wooden ruler over a pencil fulcrum to lift a book, modeling a simple lever.
Trace the food path from mouth -> esophagus -> stomach -> small intestine -> large intestine.
Compare properties of materials (conductors vs insulators, transparent vs opaque).

levels.selfPractice: Identify the simple machine (lever, inclined plane, pulley) in everyday classroom tools.

levels.name: Separation of mixtures, motion, plants

teacherActivity.title: Filter paper and pendulum swing
steps: Separate sand and water using a paper funnel and filter paper.
Demonstrate periodic motion using a weighted string pendulum.
Examine leaf venation (parallel in grass vs reticulate in peepal) and relate to root types.

levels.selfPractice: List appropriate separation methods for salt water, rice with stones, and tea leaves.

levels.name: Acids and bases, heat, nutrition in plants

teacherActivity.title: Turmeric indicator test
steps: Dip turmeric paper into lemon juice (acid, stays yellow) and soap solution (base, turns deep red).
Explain conduction along a metal spoon vs convection in heated water.
Discuss photosynthesis formula: sunlight + chlorophyll + carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen.

levels.selfPractice: Test home substances (vinegar, baking soda, lime juice) with turmeric indicator paper.

levels.name: Force, pressure, cells, chemical changes

teacherActivity.title: Onion peel cell and balloon pressure
steps: Observe onion epidermis under microscope to see cell wall, nucleus, and cytoplasm.
Press a sharp pin vs a blunt wooden block against clay to show Pressure = Force / Area.
Mix vinegar and baking soda to observe effervescence of CO2 gas as a chemical change.

levels.selfPractice: Differentiate plant cells from animal cells in a comparative two-column table.

levels.name: Atoms and molecules, motion, tissues

teacherActivity.title: Bohr atom model and ticker tape motion
steps: Build atomic models of carbon and oxygen with clay balls (protons, neutrons, electrons).
Calculate speed and acceleration from distance-time tables.
Examine permanent slides of plant tissues (xylem, phloem) and animal tissues (epithelial, muscle).

levels.selfPractice: Calculate molecular mass of water (H2O) and carbon dioxide (CO2) from atomic masses.

levels.name: Chemical reactions, electricity, life processes

teacherActivity.title: Simple circuit and displacement reaction
steps: Dip an iron nail into blue copper sulfate solution to witness displacement and color change to green.
Build a series circuit with bulb, key, and dry cell; measure voltage with multimeter.
Trace human nephron structure and function in kidney filtration.

levels.selfPractice: Balance chemical equations and solve Ohm's law calculations (V = IR).

living_characteristic_error.label: Confused living vs non-living characteristics
living_characteristic_error.explanation: Living things grow, breathe, need food/water, and reproduce. Non-living objects do not.

body_part_function_error.label: Body organ function misidentified
body_part_function_error.explanation: Different organs perform specific tasks: eyes see, lungs breathe, heart pumps blood, stomach digests.

habitat_adaptation_confusion.label: Animal habitat or physical adaptation confused
habitat_adaptation_confusion.explanation: Animals have physical traits suited to their habitats (e.g. fins and gills for water, thick fur for polar cold).

herbivore_carnivore_omnivore.label: Feeding classification confused
herbivore_carnivore_omnivore.explanation: Herbivores eat only plants, carnivores eat only other animals, and omnivores eat both plants and animals.

plant_part_function_confusion.label: Plant organ function confused
plant_part_function_confusion.explanation: Roots absorb water/nutrients and anchor; stems transport; leaves perform photosynthesis; flowers produce seeds.

food_nutrient_group_confusion.label: Nutrient group or function confused
food_nutrient_group_confusion.explanation: Carbohydrates & fats provide energy; proteins build and repair tissues; vitamins & minerals protect against disease.

states_of_matter_confusion.label: Physical state of matter or phase change confused
states_of_matter_confusion.explanation: Solids have definite shape and volume; liquids flow with definite volume; gases expand to fill any container.

organ_system_function_error.label: Organ system responsibility confused
organ_system_function_error.explanation: Circulatory transports blood, respiratory exchanges gases, digestive breaks down food, nervous controls responses.

simple_machine_confusion.label: Type of simple machine misidentified
simple_machine_confusion.explanation: Six simple machines: lever, pulley, wheel & axle, inclined plane, wedge, and screw.

mixture_separation_error.label: Separation technique does not match properties
mixture_separation_error.explanation: Filtration separates insoluble solids from liquids; evaporation recovers dissolved solutes; distillation separates based on boiling points.

acids_bases_indicators.label: Acidic vs basic property or indicator color confused
acids_bases_indicators.explanation: Acids turn blue litmus red and taste sour; bases turn red litmus blue, feel soapy, and taste bitter.

heat_transfer_mode_confusion.label: Conduction, convection, or radiation confused
heat_transfer_mode_confusion.explanation: Conduction transfers heat through direct contact in solids; convection through fluids; radiation through electromagnetic waves.

force_motion_law_error.label: Force, friction, or Newton's law misinterpreted
force_motion_law_error.explanation: Friction opposes relative motion between surfaces; balanced forces result in zero net acceleration.

cell_organelle_confusion.label: Cell organelle function confused
cell_organelle_confusion.explanation: Mitochondria release energy (ATP); chloroplasts photosynthesize in plants; nucleus stores genetic DNA.

atomic_molecular_confusion.label: Atoms, molecules, or subatomic particles confused
atomic_molecular_confusion.explanation: Protons and neutrons reside in the nucleus, surrounded by electrons in shells. An element contains identical atoms.

chemical_vs_physical_change.label: Physical change confused with chemical reaction
chemical_vs_physical_change.explanation: Physical changes alter state or appearance without creating new substances; chemical reactions form new chemical bonds.

circuit_electricity_error.label: Open vs closed circuit or Ohm's law relation confused
circuit_electricity_error.explanation: Current flows only in a closed complete circuit; electric current is the flow of electric charge (electrons).

respiration_photosynthesis_reversal.label: Photosynthesis confused with cellular respiration
respiration_photosynthesis_reversal.explanation: Photosynthesis consumes CO2 and water to produce glucose and O2; respiration consumes glucose and O2 to produce energy and CO2.
